From 6dd2d4ad9c8429523b1c220c5132bd551c006425 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 13:17:37 -0300
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/mana: Validate rx_hash_key_len

Sashiko points out that rx_hash_key_len comes from a uAPI structure and is
blindly passed to memcpy, allowing the userspace to trash kernel
memory. Bounds check it so the memcpy cannot overflow.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 0266a177631d ("RDMA/mana_ib: Add a driver for Microsoft Azure Network Adapter")
Link: https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/0-v2-1c49eeb88c48%2B91-rdma_udata_rep_jgg%40nvidia.com?part=1
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/r/4-v1-41f3135e5565+9d2-rdma_ai_fixes1_jgg@nvidia.com
Reviewed-by: Long Li <longli@microsoft.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c
index 645581359cee..f7bb0d1f0f80 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c
@@ -21,6 +21,9 @@ static int mana_ib_cfg_vport_steering(struct mana_ib_dev *dev,
 
 	gc = mdev_to_gc(dev);
 
+	if (rx_hash_key_len > sizeof(req->hashkey))
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	req_buf_size = struct_size(req, indir_tab, MANA_INDIRECT_TABLE_DEF_SIZE);
 	req = kzalloc(req_buf_size, GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!req)
-- 
2.34.1

The patch adds a validation check for the `rx_hash_key_len` field in the `mana_ib_cfg_vport_steering` function within `drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c`. The fix prevents a potential buffer overflow by ensuring that the value does not exceed the size of the destination buffer `req->hashkey` before it is used in a `memcpy` operation. This addresses a security vulnerability where user-supplied data from a uAPI structure could otherwise lead to memory corruption.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
if (rx_hash_key_len)
        memcpy(req->hashkey, rx_hash_key, rx_hash_key_len);
```
Reason:
The `rx_hash_key_len` is supplied by userspace via a uAPI structure and is used directly in `memcpy` without any bounds check. If the user provides a value larger than the size of `req->hashkey` (which is a fixed-size buffer), the `memcpy` overflows the destination buffer, corrupting kernel memory.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
if (rx_hash_key_len > sizeof(req->hashkey))
        return -EINVAL;
```
Reason:
This check compares `rx_hash_key_len` against the actual size of the destination buffer (`sizeof(req->hashkey)`). If the length exceeds the buffer capacity, the function returns an error (`-EINVAL`) before the `memcpy` is ever executed, thus preventing the buffer overflow.
